html:
Amul is a dairy cooperative founded in 1946 in Anand, Gujarat, owned by the farmers who sell it milk. It became the model for India's White Revolution in milk.

In the 1940s farmers of Kaira district sold milk to a private dairy that supplied Bombay and paid them little. Advised by Vallabhbhai Patel and led by Tribhuvandas Patel, they formed their own union in 1946. The young engineer Verghese Kurien joined in 1949 and ran it for decades.

The Anand pattern worked like this:

  • Village societies collected milk twice a day and paid farmers at once, by fat content.
  • A district union processed it into milk, butter and cheese.
  • The union sold under one brand, Amul.

In 1970 Kurien took the model national through Operation Flood, linking village cooperatives across India to city markets. India became the world's largest milk producer. The story was told in the 1976 film Manthan, paid for by half a million farmers. Amul is now one of India's best known brands, a food revolution that ran beside the Green Revolution.
sum: Amul is a dairy cooperative founded in 1946 in Anand, Gujarat, owned by the farmers who sell it milk. It became the model for India's White Revolution in milk.
